course_description.character: The organizer-linked 2027 registration and timing page confirms an 82km paved island route from Punat through Krk town, Malinska, Njivice, Omišalj, Dobrinj and Vrbnik toward Baška. The latest official elevation and climb reference remains the 2026 course: 1,320m with four categorized ascents, including Treskavac Pass and the return climb toward Punat. The final 2027 organizer rulebook overrides those historical climbing details.

The latest climb-level reference is the 2026 Vrbnik-side ascent to Treskavac Pass followed by the descent into Baška; final 2027 elevation and climb details remain pending.

history.origin_story: Inaugural edition held in Punat on April 27, 2024, organized by Hoteli Punat/Falkensteiner Punat with support from the Punat Tourist Board; Marin Kirin and Toni Dujmenović have directed the race since. Run with the Croatian Cycling Federation and Granfondo World Tour, though it is not a UCI Gran Fondo World Series qualifier.
history.reputation: A young but quickly-sold-out event — the 2026 field cap was reached about six weeks before race day.

biased_opinion.verdict: Real, Young, Popular — But Read the Fine Print
biased_opinion.summary: The organizer's embedded RaceResult event confirms the fourth Krk Gran Fondo for Saturday, April 24, 2027, while the organizer-linked registration and timing page confirms an 82km route from Punat across Krk toward Baška, six advance-price windows, no event-day registration, and a 600-rider cap. Sources for 2026 variously report 400 actual starters, roughly 450 expected riders, and a 500-place registration allocation, so historical field reporting remains inconsistent. The latest elevation and climb reference is still the 2026 rolling-island course with 1,320m and four categorized climbs. The 2026 paperwork also has real document-control problems: its propositions PDF misprints the year, inconsistently rounds the distance, and carries over a stray Zadar reference. Treat the 2027 date, distance, town sequence, pricing, and cap as current; treat elevation, climb, feed-zone, and cutoff specifics as provisional until the final 2027 rulebook appears.
strengths: The organizer-linked sources confirm Saturday, April 24, 2027, an 82km route, six advance-price windows, and a 600-rider cap
The 2027 town sequence establishes a real island crossing from Punat toward Baška rather than a generic coastal loop
Post-race coverage reports extensive road control and a 190-person event operating team
Adriatic island route through Malinska, Njivice, Omišalj, Dobrinj, Vrbnik and Baška
weaknesses: Official race-propositions PDF has real document-control problems (wrong year printed, distance rounding inconsistencies, a leftover Zadar reference) — don't take the PDF as gospel over the live event page
Riders 40+ minutes behind the leader at the km-52 control are diverted to a shortened finish — stricter than typical recreational-fondo pacing
Not a UCI Gran Fondo World Series qualifier, unlike nearby Istria Gran Fondo — lower competitive prestige
Young event (3rd edition in 2026) with a correspondingly thin track record
Final 2027 elevation, categorized climbs, feed zones, cutoff policy and start schedule remain unpublished
biased_opinion.bottom_line: The April 24, 2027 date and 82km island route are confirmed well enough to build a race-specific training plan. Use the 2026 elevation and climb profile only as demand context, and replace it if the final 2027 rulebook changes the course.

final_verdict.one_liner: A confirmed 82km Krk Island crossing on April 24, 2027, with the final climbing and operating rules still pending.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Put it on the calendar if a compact Adriatic island road race appeals to you. Train for 82km of rolling paved terrain and repeated climbing, but keep exact pacing, feed-zone and cutoff decisions provisional until the organizer publishes the final 2027 rulebook; the 1,320m total and four categorized climbs are the latest 2026 reference.
final_verdict.alternatives: For a longer, UCI-qualifying Croatian gran fondo: Istria Gran Fondo (Umag, 105km, UCI Gran Fondo World Series). For another Adriatic island event: Granfondo Pag - Cycling on the Moon (Novalja, ~107km/1,210m).
